passage: Someone I only knew from a game chat sent me a message: "Which colony do you live in? Send me your address, I'll post you a sticker." I did not answer right away. It felt off, but they had been friendly for weeks, so I was not sure. I called my cousin Karthik, who is in college. "Never share it," Karthik said. "Not even a little bit. Block them." So I blocked the contact, and then I showed my father the chat on his phone. He said thank you for telling him and sat with me while we went through my settings. - Raghav

passage:
Note to Eshaan's class teacher, Wednesday
Ma'am, I want you to know about something from last night, since the class uses the same game. A player Eshaan did not know had been chatting with him for a few days and then asked for our home address, "to send a prize." Eshaan felt unsure. Before answering, he called his older cousin Vinita, who told him clearly: never share an address with anyone online. He blocked the player and came to me straight away. I sat with him, told him he had done nothing wrong and that coming to me was exactly right. We took a screenshot, reported the account in the game, and I rang the cyber helpline the same evening.
- Eshaan's father

qa.q: What did the player say the address was for?
How did Eshaan feel when the player asked for the address?
qa.a: He felt unsure and uneasy, which is why he checked with his cousin before answering.

qa.q: What else could the family do to keep Eshaan safe online?
qa.a: They could agree that any request for personal details always goes to a parent first, and keep game chats on settings that limit strangers.

qa.q: How does the request look to Vinita?
qa.a: Vinita sees clear danger in it and gives a firm, simple rule, helping her younger cousin act quickly.

grounding: It shows a boy unsure about an online stranger's request for his address checking with an older cousin, blocking the contact and telling his father.

Thursday
Diary, something weird happened in my game chat. A player called StarKing99 has been friendly for a week. Today he said, "Send me your address, I'll post you a gift card. Don't tell your parents, it's our secret." I almost did. Then I thought, why is it a secret? I messaged Rukmini didi, my cousin in college. She wrote back fast: "NEVER share your address. Block him and tell your dad right now." So I blocked him and told Papa. Papa didn't get angry. He said, "Good boy, Raghav. You did right to tell me. It's not your fault." We reported the account together and he called the helpline before dinner.
- Raghav
